title: fix(libpod): keep '=' in a volume subpath
body:
The `subpath` mount option is parsed with `strings.Split(o, "=")[1]`, which keeps only the text between the first and second `=`. A subpath containing `=` is therefore truncated, and the container gets a different directory mounted than the one that was asked for.

```
--mount type=volume,src=v,dst=/mnt,subpath=/opt/a=b/c    mounts /opt/a
```

`=` is a legal character in a Linux directory name, and every layer above this line already preserves it:

| layer | how it handles `=` |
|---|---|
| CLI (`pkg/specgenutil/volumes.go`) | `strings.Cut(arg, "=")`, keeps the remainder in the value |
| `pkg/util/mount_opts.go` | passes the option string through untouched |
| `pkg/specgen/generate/kube/kube.go` | re-formats with `fmt.Sprintf("subpath=%s", ...)` |
| compat API (`containers_create.go`) | same, via `addField` |

This one line is the only place the rest of the path is dropped, and it is reachable from all three of those entry points: CLI `--mount`, the Docker-compat API, and Kubernetes YAML `subPath`.

The read is confined to the volume by `pathrs.OpenInRoot`, so this is a wrong directory rather than an escape. When the truncated path does not exist, the error names a path the user never typed, which is the confusing case.

`strings.CutPrefix` replaces the `HasPrefix` test and the index in one step, so the guard and the extraction can no longer disagree.

Added an e2e case alongside the existing subpath test, using a subpath with an `=` in it and asserting the expected file is visible in the mount.

**Not verified by a local build:** this tree needs the cgo gpgme bindings and there is no C toolchain on my machine. Baseline `main` fails the same way on the same package, so the failure is environmental rather than caused by this change. `gofmt` is clean on both files and CI has to confirm the compile.
